title: Job’s wife: one sentence in the KJV, a speech of six lines in the Greek
summary: In the KJV, with the Hebrew, Job’s wife says one sentence. Brenton’s Greek says that much time had passed and gives her a longer speech about her dead children, Job sitting in the open air among worms, and her own life as a wandering servant.
text: KJV Job 2:9: “Then said his wife unto him, Dost thou still retain thine integrity? curse God, and die.” Hebrew (WLC) 2:9: וַתֹּ֤אמֶר לֹו֙ אִשְׁתֹּ֔ו עֹדְךָ֖ מַחֲזִ֣יק בְּתֻמָּתֶ֑ךָ בָּרֵ֥ךְ אֱלֹהִ֖ים וָמֻֽת. Septuagint (Brenton Greek), printed under the labels 9 and 9a to 9e. 9: Χρόνου δὲ πολλοῦ προβεβηκότος, εἶπεν αὐτῷ ἡ γυνὴ αὐτοῦ, μέχρι τίνος καρτερήσεις, λέγων, [and when much time had gone by, his wife said to him, How long wilt thou hold out, saying,] 9a: ἰδοὺ ἀναμένω χρόνον ἔτι μικρὸν, προσδεχόμενος τὴν ἐλπίδα τῆς σωτηρίας μου; [Behold, I wait yet a little time, looking for the hope of my deliverance?] 9b: ἰδοὺ γὰρ ἠφάνισταί σου τὸ μνημόσυνον ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς· υἱοὶ καὶ θυγατέρες, ἐμῆς κοιλίας ὠδῖνες καὶ πόνοι, οὓς εἰς τὸ κενὸν ἐκοπίασα μετὰ μόχθων· [for behold, thy memorial is blotted out from the earth: sons and daughters, the pangs and pains of my womb, for whom I laboured in vain with toils;] 9c: σύ τε αὐτὸς ἐν σαπρίᾳ σκωλήκων κάθησαι διανυκτερεύων αἴθριος, [and thou thyself sittest in the rottenness of worms, passing the night in the open air,] 9d: κᾀγὼ πλανωμένη καὶ λάτρις τόπον ἐκ τόπου καὶ οἰκίαν ἐξ οἰκίας, προσδεχομένη τὸν ἥλιον πότε δύσεται, ἵνα ἀναπαύσωμαι τῶν μόχθων μου καὶ τῶν ὀδυνῶν αἵ με νῦν συνέχουσιν· [and I a wanderer and a hired servant from place to place and from house to house, waiting for when the sun will set, that I may rest from my toils and from the pains that now hold me;] 9e: ἀλλὰ εἶπόν τι ῥῆμα εἰς Κύριον, καὶ τελεύτα. title: “My redeemer liveth … in my flesh shall I see God” — the Greek has no seeing of God
summary: In the KJV Job knows that his redeemer lives and will stand on the earth, and that in his flesh he will see God. In Brenton’s Greek he knows that the one who is about to release him is everlasting, to raise up on the earth his skin; the Greek of these verses has no clause about seeing God.
text: KJV Job 19:25: “For I know that my redeemer liveth, and that he shall stand at the latter day upon the earth:” KJV 19:26: “And though after my skin worms destroy this body, yet in my flesh shall I see God:” Hebrew (WLC) 19:25: וַאֲנִ֣י יָ֭דַעְתִּי גֹּ֣אֲלִי חָ֑י וְ֝אַחֲרֹ֗ון עַל־עָפָ֥ר יָקֽוּם. 19:26: וְאַחַ֣ר עֹ֖ורִֽי נִקְּפוּ־זֹ֑את וּ֝מִבְּשָׂרִ֗י אֶֽחֱזֶ֥ה אֱלֹֽוהַּ; the last two words are [I shall see God]. Septuagint (Brenton Greek) 19:25: Οἶδα γὰρ ὅτι ἀένναός ἐστιν ὁ ἐκλύειν με μέλλων, [For I know that he is everlasting who is about to release me,] 19:26: ἐπὶ γῆς ἀναστῆσαι τὸ δέρμα μου τὸ ἀναντλοῦν ταῦτα· παρὰ γὰρ Κυρίου ταῦτά μοι συνετελέσθη, [to raise up upon the earth my skin that bears these things; for from the Lord these things were accomplished for me,] 19:27: ἃ ἐγὼ ἐμαυτῷ συνεπίσταμαι, ἃ ὁ ὀφθαλμός μου ἑώρακε, καὶ οὐκ ἄλλος [which I am conscious of in myself, which my eye has seen, and not another]; KJV 19:27: “Whom I shall see for myself, and mine eyes shall behold, and not another” Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/18/19/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/JOB19.htm.
reasoning: Three things differ. The KJV’s redeemer “shall stand at the latter day upon the earth”; the Greek has no standing and no latter day, and its “upon the earth” belongs to the raising of Job’s skin. The KJV has “worms destroy this body”; the Greek has neither. The KJV, with the Hebrew, has Job say that he will see God; the Greek of 19:26 and 19:27 as quoted has no word for seeing God, and names the Lord as the one from whom “these things” were accomplished.
scope: G applies at 19:25 and 19:26. Both texts speak of one who will act for Job, and the Greek speaks of a raising up; the difference recorded is in what is said to happen and in whether Job says he will see God.
